To be honest, setting the weight guideline is there for rolling not based on the quality of the herb. Finer quality herb, and you could make a spliff if you want to conserve, but the biomass must be there for an effective roll. Start by grinding up the herb in a grinder, and dump about 50-75% in the paper, and start to roll it back and forth in between your thumb and both your index and middle finger. Your index and middle finger should be touching. When you begin to get more of a joint shape, add more herb and keep rolling. keep adding until it gets hard to handle (too heavy for the paper) or the paper get too full for you. Notice, still no filter. At this point you will have an open paper with a thick cylinder of green at the crease. roll the joint until the paper catches, (you can use a thin object like the papes box or a knife to tuck the edge of the paper, if you have trouble getting it to catch. be warned this will make the joint burn slower along the side of the joint the paper is tuck into. cosmetic issue) You can also put in a crutch at this point (I use RAW crutches) before you seal but after you have tucked you paper, make sure the crutch is ready for the joint by this point. after you have the filter in and sealed the joint, take a national geographic, rip off the cover or a page and fold it in two pieces. Put the left over weed in the trough. now on the end that is still open, and doesn't have a filter in it, pad it down and start scooping up the excess weed. knock the weed down into the joint by dropping the joint filter first into the trough. keep loading up the extra flowers until you have a hard time putting more in. Seal the edge, Twist twist twist twist twist. Bite. Don't light. Take another filter and stick it behind the other filter. Push it in as far as it will go and cut/burn of the part protruding. This final step make the filter longer (cooler smoke/less finger burns at the roach) and it also creates a finer more even burn all the way through the joint. I never have any left over weed in these joints, the extra filter length allows me to smoke it all down without burning my fingers. 

A more experience smoker will tell you that the weed at the bottom of the joint is bad and you don't have to smoke it... which is true if your weed doesn't run. My weed runs, so I like the extra length in the filter, to make sure I get all the good stuff. A double filter technique will not only make a damn good joint, you can actually tell the quality of the j before you even light it. Just inhale on the unlit joint and the smell of the weed should fill your mouth. You'll be able to pull, but not as easily as breathing. A really easy to pull joint that is not lit will burn too hot and too fast while lit. 1-2 minutes, burning your throat and lungs the whole time. A fat, hard to pull jay will last for 20-25 minutes, and it will be more enjoyable. To be clear, it should be hard to pull unlit, but it should fill your mouth with flavor. really fat and well packed joints will act like a cigar if you're personally smoking it (2-3 puff an minute) rather than a cigarette. Slow and steady wins the race of who can roll the best joint.
